facts.fact: Agence Ecofin states that the Central African Republic has two terrestrial fibre links with its neighbours today, the routes through Cameroon and Congo-Brazzaville, carried by the roughly 935 km Central African Backbone network.
The article says CAR authorities estimated in May 2026 that connecting the country to submarine cables through the terrestrial networks of coastal countries had markedly improved available speeds.

On 8 October 2026 in Moscow the CAR and DRC digital ministers agreed on the need to carry out the CAR-DRC fibre interconnection, which would reach the Moanda submarine cable landing; no timetable or financing agreement was announced.
The article says CAR drew closer to South Sudan around a connectivity project announced in May 2026; its route, timetable and technical terms have not been detailed.
